fields.features_heading: What Emergent Puts Into a Diet Quiz
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the quiz, the matching logic, and the table behind it from one prompt, and a follow-up prompt changes any of them.
fields.feature_1:
Matching questions from one prompt

Describe the patterns you want to match, such as a planner or a grazer. Emergent drafts the questions, maps each option to a pattern, and rewords any of them by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
A result screen for every pattern

Each result gets a title and a short description that reads as a preference, not a verdict. Takers see their match, what it means, and what the next step with you is.
fields.feature_3:
Email capture before the result

Ask for an email on the last screen and the app holds the result until it is entered. Every address lands beside that taker's answers, ready for your follow-up list.
fields.feature_4:
Every answer in a database you own

Each finished quiz is a row: the answers, the matched pattern, the email, and a timestamp. Filter the rows by pattern before a launch, or export them whenever you need to.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

Takers answer one question at a time with a progress bar, built for thumbs on a phone and easy to finish between meetings. Emergent puts no cap on how many people respond.
fields.feature_6:
Code and a domain that stay yours

The quiz runs on your own domain, which Emergent includes and bills in credits. Paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository, and the next campaign starts from it.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Teams Put a Diet Quiz to Work
fields.tab_content_1:
64 matched The Planner in March

Larkglen Nutrition matches every quiz taker to an eating pattern. In March, 212 people finished the quiz: 64 matched The Planner, 58 The Grazer, 49 The Winger, and 41 The Social Eater. Each Planner match got an invite to the structured coaching track, and every answer sits in the studio's own database.
fields.tab_content_2:
448 takers typed an email to see a result

Rowanmere Kitchen sells weekly meal boxes and runs a box finder quiz on its site. The last screen asks for an email, and the result stays locked until an address goes in. 1,180 people finished the quiz and 448 left an address, each one saved beside the box they matched.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every score under 6 ends in a call

Granite Row Fitness gives every new member a short habit quiz at signup, and the app turns the answers into a habit score. A score under 6 books a trainer call, with the member's answers on the trainer's screen before it starts. Of the 31 who joined in April, 9 scored under 6.
fields.tab_content_4:
1,468 readers finished it on their phones

The Weekly Table sends a scored quiz to its readers with the Friday issue, 7 questions and a result band at the end. Last Friday, 2,406 readers opened it and 1,468 finished on their phones. The editor watches finishes land on a live dashboard.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Diet Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a diet quiz that matches takers to an eating pattern, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the job the quiz does
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write the results before the questions
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Draft questions that split the patterns
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what a finished quiz earns you before you write anything, such as coaching leads or intake scores. One quiz does one job well. Put that job in your prompt, and Emergent builds the quiz and the table behind it around that goal.
fields.howto_step_2_des: A matching quiz maps every option to a result, which suits eating patterns and product picks. A scored quiz counts points and fits habit checks with bands at the end. Name the type in the prompt before any questions exist.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Draft each result as a short preference, such as a planner who shops once and cooks from a list. When the results are clear, every question has a target, and takers get a result that reads like them rather than a grade.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask about behavior, not goals: who cooks, when, and what a usual week holds. A good question sends different takers to different options. If every taker picks the same answer, the question splits nothing, so cut it or sharpen the options.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Gate the result with an email
fields.howto_step_5_des: Add an email field on the last screen and say what the address gets: a link back to the result plus one follow-up, nothing more. The result itself stays in the app, which writes each address into the same row as its answers.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it with 5 people before launch
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the draft to 5 people who match your audience and watch where they stall. A question read two ways, an option nobody picks, a result that feels wrong: each shows up in minutes. Fix the wording by prompt and send it again.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Watch the results table and prune
fields.howto_step_7_des: Check the table after the first 100 takers. A pattern almost nobody matches needs sharper questions, or should fold into a neighbor. Retire options that never get picked, and keep the quiz short enough to finish in one sitting.

faq_plan.a: A diet quiz is a short set of questions about how someone eats, turned into a result such as an eating pattern or a habit score. Coaches and meal brands use one to match people to a program or a product, and publishers run them to keep readers engaged.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a diet quiz?
faq_plan.a: Describe the quiz in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder: the patterns or score bands you want, the tone of the questions, and where answers should land. Emergent builds it from that prompt, and another prompt rewords a question or adds a pattern.

faq_plan.q: What diet is best for me free quiz?
faq_plan.ref: What diet is best for me free quiz?

prov.original: What diet is best for me free quiz?

faq_plan.a: Try the quiz on this page: 8 questions that match you to 1 of 4 eating patterns, with no signup. A quiz cannot tell you what to eat; it shows the pattern your answers lean toward. To publish a free diet quiz of your own, Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What diet quiz questions should I ask?
faq_plan.a: Write questions a taker can answer without thinking hard: a normal weeknight, a grocery run, eating out. Each question should separate at least two patterns, and every option should map to one result. A love language quiz runs on the same matching mechanics; only the subject changes.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a diet quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Keep it between 6 and 10. Fewer than 6 gives the match little to work with; more than 10 asks a lot of someone on a phone. The quiz on this page runs 8 questions. If a question never changes anyone's result, it is padding: cut it.

faq_plan.q: How does a diet quiz match someone to an eating pattern?
faq_plan.a: Every option quietly points at one pattern. When someone finishes, the app counts the points per pattern and shows the one with the most; a tie goes to the result listed first. That is why options matter more than questions: each one is a small vote.

faq_plan.q: How do I get leads from a diet quiz?
faq_plan.a: Hold each result behind an email field, then send one follow-up that links back to the result page. The email carries no result details. A quiz funnel takes it further: the result screen routes every pattern to its own offer. Emergent puts no response caps on a quiz, however big the traffic gets.

faq_plan.q: Do I need a nutritionist to make a diet quiz?
faq_plan.a: Not to build one. Setting up a quiz takes no nutrition credential. Keep results as preferences, such as a pattern your answers lean toward, and keep medical claims out of the copy. If the quiz feeds a coaching or nutrition business, have the practitioner review the results text before launch.

faq_plan.q: What should the result screen of a diet quiz say?
faq_plan.a: Three things: the name of the match, two or three sentences describing it in the taker's own terms, and one next step. Write it so a taker would happily screenshot it, and skip scores unless the quiz promised one. On Emergent, the result screen changes with one more prompt.

faq_plan.q: Where should a diet quiz live on my site?
faq_plan.a: Give the quiz its own page and link it from the places your audience already reads, such as recipe posts and the newsletter. Keep the pattern names visible above the start button, since they are the hook. The same placement thinking applies to a spirit animal quiz or any other matching format.

quiz.title: Diet Quiz: Which Eating Pattern Fits Your Week?
quiz.intro: Eight questions about how a normal week of eating goes. Your result names the pattern your answers lean toward, with one idea to build on it.

questions.text: How does a weeknight dinner usually get decided?

options.text: It was planned at the weekend
It grows out of snacks through the evening
I open the fridge and see what works
Whoever I am eating with picks

questions.text: What does your grocery run look like?

options.text: One big shop from a written list
Small top-ups every couple of days
Whatever looks good when I walk in
A shared list the household adds to

questions.text: How many times do you eat on a busy workday?

options.text: Three meals at set times
Five or six small bites
It changes a lot from day to day
Mostly when others take a break

questions.text: Your fridge on a Wednesday holds:

options.text: Labeled containers for the next few days
Cut fruit, yogurt, and quick bites
A mix of half-used ingredients
Leftovers from a shared dinner

questions.text: What breaks your eating routine most?

options.text: A plan falling apart midweek
Long gaps without a snack nearby
Having a routine in the first place
Plans with friends or family

questions.text: Which kitchen tool earns its spot?

options.text: A set of meal prep containers
A good snack drawer
One big pan that does everything
A table with room for guests

questions.text: Pick the meal that sounds best tonight.

options.text: The dish I prepped on Sunday
A plate of small things to pick at
Something new I have never cooked
A long dinner with people I like

questions.text: What would make healthy eating easier for you?

options.text: A plan I can repeat each week
Better options within arm's reach
Simple ideas I can adapt on the spot
People around me eating the same way

results.title: The Planner
results.description: Your answers lean toward structure: a list, a shop, and meals decided ahead. Build on it with a weekly template you can swap a dish or two in without starting over.

results.title: The Grazer
results.description: Your answers lean toward smaller, more frequent bites through the day. Build on it by keeping a few ready options within reach, so the next bite is an easy choice.

results.title: The Winger
results.description: Your answers lean toward deciding in the moment and cooking with what is there. Build on it with a short list of go-to combinations that work with whatever is in the fridge.

results.title: The Social Eater
results.description: Your answers lean toward meals shaped by the people around you. Build on it by suggesting one shared dish each week that everyone at the table enjoys.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Diet Quiz That Matches People to an Eating Pattern'; hero 'Build a diet quiz that matches each taker to an eating pattern, saved to a database you own, or play the 8-question quiz below.' covers the whole job.

intent.evidence: AMBER angle carried: playable 8-question matching quiz on the page for takers, plus builder copy for makers; FAQ 3 'Try the quiz on this page: 8 questions that match you to 1 of 4 eating patterns'.

specificity.evidence: why_table is the general survey set (SurveyMonkey, Microsoft Forms, SurveyHero; 'Survey builder with templates, including employee engagement') on a quiz page; Divit 2026-11-11 decision 3 requires the quiz-maker set.

openers.evidence: Paragraphs open on full sentences: 'Larkglen Nutrition matches every quiz taker to an eating pattern.', 'Describe the patterns you want to match, such as a planner or a grazer.'

craft.evidence: Two ', so' endings (under the cap); sentences vary: 'One quiz does one job well.'

voice.evidence: Concrete and calm: 'If every taker picks the same answer, the question splits nothing'; no AI tells found.

truth.evidence: FAQ 8 'No, as long as the quiz recommends rather than prescribes' states a professional/legal standard with no domain source; feature_5 'keeps a 10-question quiz under 3 minutes on a phone' unsourced timing fact; howto_step_5_des 'say what the address gets: the result plus one follow-up' and FAQ 7 'send one follow-up tied to the pattern that taker matched' put a taker's eating result in email. Tab numbers check: 64+58+49+41=212, 448/1,180=38%, 1,468/2,406=61%.

distinct.evidence: Own eating-pattern vocabulary (Planner, Grazer, Winger, Social Eater) and four distinct segments: coaching, meal boxes, gym intake, newsletter.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, hub link in item 2, sibling links (love language quiz, spirit animal quiz), F9 moat lines in FAQ 3, 7, 9; FAQ 8 truth issue scored under truth.

images.evidence: Tab images match copy: bars 64/58/49/41 and 212 takers; 448 of 1,180 with locked result; habit score < 6 rule with 9 of 31; 1,468 of 2,406 and Question 5 of 7. No health details in transit drawn.

findings.issue: A quiz page (playable spec.quiz, primary 'diet quiz') carries the hub's general survey table, the default the quiz-maker category set replaced (Divit 2026-11-11 decision 3: new quiz pages use the quiz-maker set). The cells talk about employee engagement and satisfaction templates on a diet quiz page, and none of the three vendors is quiz software.
findings.fix: Regenerate with `hubctl table <url>` without --vs so the quiz-maker set (ProProfs, Interact, Typeform ... with the build row) is used; do not hand-edit.

findings.quote: No, as long as the quiz recommends rather than prescribes.
findings.issue: States when a nutrition professional is or is not required (a professional and legal standard; dietetics practice rules vary by US state) with no spec.domain_sources entry (domain_sources is empty). On a YMYL health page it also tells the reader the quiz may 'recommend', against the page's own preference-only framing.
findings.fix: Answer without asserting a legal or professional rule, or source it. For example: answer that building the quiz needs no nutrition credential in Emergent, keep results as eating-pattern preferences with no advice on what to eat, and have a registered dietitian review any nutrition wording before launch. Or replace the question with another on-topic written question.

findings.quote: which keeps a 10-question quiz under 3 minutes on a phone
findings.issue: A completion-time fact (and a causal claim that the progress bar produces it) with no domain source and beyond the 'conversational' claim, which covers one-question-per-screen flows only.
findings.fix: Drop the timing claim and keep the approved capability, e.g. 'Takers answer one question per screen with a progress bar, built for thumbs on a phone.' Keep the body within 165-182 characters.

findings.quote: say what the address gets: the result plus one follow-up, nothing more
findings.issue: Tells the builder to email the taker's diet quiz result. On this health page (YMYL), a person's eating result must stay in the app; email may only say a result is ready and link to it.
findings.fix: Say the address gets a link back to the result on the site plus one follow-up, and the result itself stays in the app.

findings.quote: Hold each result behind an email field, then send one follow-up tied to the pattern that taker matched.
findings.issue: A follow-up email whose content is keyed to the taker's eating pattern carries that result in transit. Same class as howto_step_5_des.
findings.fix: Send one follow-up that links to the taker's result page or offer page, with no eating details in the email itself; the per-pattern offer can live on the result screen ('the result screen routes every pattern to its own offer' already says this).

findings.quote: the app turns the answers into a habit score. A score under 6 books a trainer call
